messages:
maya: Quick question — audit flagged telemetry traces containing user identifiers. I'm thinking about doing attribute-level encryption in the collector so exporters never see raw PII. Anyone have concerns with searchability / console UX?

jon: Prefer collector-side is good for minimizing blast radius. Main downside is we lose ability to index those attributes in the console (filters, per-route dashboards).

ana: Is the ask to keep traces for 2 years but remove direct identifiers? If so we need a way to map for legal hold requests without exposing raw values.

security-bot: Checklist: 1) identify attributes with PII 2) define retention + audit TTL 3) KMS-based envelope encryption w/ key-rotation policy 4) logging of key access for SOC2. See: https://redwood.internal/compliance/telemetry-guidelines 

maya: Right — proposal: collector encrypts selected attributes using envelope encryption with customer-managed KMS key (or Redwood KMS for internal). Store deterministic ciphertext for things we might want to join on, and non-deterministic for everything else.

jon: Heads-up: deterministic encryption allows equality joins but leaks frequency. Might be acceptable for hashed ids but not emails. Also it will break current log/trace search that relies on plain text. UX will need a 'masked attribute' filter.

devex-sam: From a UX perspective we could surface a special filter that matches on 'encrypted:<attribute>' and fall back to metadata counts. But customers will expect reasonable query latency; adding decryption-to-search will be expensive unless we index ciphertexts at ingest.

sam: Tech notes from infra: OTLP collector can run a processor before exporters. Example sketch: 
```yaml
processors:
  attribute_encrypter:
    algorithm: AES-GCM
    deterministic_attributes: ["user.id"]
    non_deterministic: ["http.request.body", "user.email"]
    kms_key: projects/redwood/locations/global/keyRings/telemetry/cryptoKeys/telemetry-wrap
```
This would wrap attribute values and replace them in spans.

ana: Two compliance flags: 1) key rotation: when we rotate, we must still be able to decrypt historical records for e-discovery. So either keep older KEKs or rewrap ciphertexts on rotation (heavy). 2) Auditability: every decryption call must be logged with requestor and justification.

maya: For the e-discovery case I was thinking we keep an access-controlled audit queue that holds rewrap requests. Rewrap could be done offline with HSM access. Not ideal but minimizes exposure in the hot path.

jon: Also consider sampling policy interactions. We currently sample spans at 1% for trace volume. If we encrypt before sampling, we could lose ability to sample based on PII presence. Maybe sample after classification but before encryption.

devex-sam: That implies the collector needs a lightweight classifier to tag traces with 'contains_pii' boolean before encrypting. We should add a config knob: classify -> sample -> encrypt -> export.

security-bot: Regs note: GDPR considers encrypted PII still personal data if keyholder can decrypt. So encryption reduces risk but doesn't absolve retention obligations. Document retention TTLs explicitly and provide data subject access controls.

maya: Good call. Action items: 
- ana: confirm legal retention window (is 2y accurate?)
- sam: prototype attribute_encrypter processor in otelcol and run perf tests on ingest latency
- devex-sam: mock console UX for encrypted-attribute filters and index strategies
- jon + security-bot: define key-rotation + audit log design

ana: I'll take retention check and loop in compliance.

sam: I'll spin up a small PoC branch and post perf numbers tomorrow.

jon: Can we include a toggle to run encryption in a 'dry-run' mode that leaves plain attributes but logs what would be encrypted? That would help us measure impact on dashboards before flip.

maya: Yes — plan to add dry-run to the processor config. Example: `dry_run: true` and `log_sample: 1%`.

security-bot: Make sure dry-run logs are redacted and stored in an access-controlled bucket.

devex-sam: If we standardize on producing deterministic ciphertext for certain keys, we can maintain lightweight inverted indexes on ciphertexts to support exact-match filters without decryption. I'll wire up a prototype with Elastic indexing of cipher values.

maya: Perfect. Thanks everyone — will follow up with a short RFC and the PoC link. :thumbsup:
